**Context resolved** (bounded pre-planning pass, orchestrator side):

- `scripts/select_step9c_tests.py` (2,834 lines) already carries an explicit
  consumer registry for exactly this class: `TRANSITIVE_CONSUMER_TESTS`
  (line 847, founding incident #1589), whose docstring names the failure mode
  verbatim — "the import arm sees no Import node (dynamic loads), the literal
  arm needs the CONTIGUOUS repo-relative path, and the stem arm needs the
  module stem in the test's FILENAME". Its most recent entry (#2412,
  `scripts/step5a_sibling_probe.py`) was added for a constructed-path
  importlib consumer. So scope item 1 has a pre-existing mechanism; the
  planner should weigh a registry entry against a general discovery arm.
- Baseline reproducer confirms the gap on `main`:
  `--map-files` for `scripts/clean_experiment_downloads.py` emits 13 pairs /
  13 tests, rc=0, and neither `tests/test_janitor_tmp_scratch_sweep.py` nor
  `tests/test_vm_disk_guard_slurm_src.py` is among them.
- **Sharper mechanism than the body's "feature-named" framing.** All three
  janitor consumer tests load the module the same way
  (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(mod_name, _SCRIPTS / f"{mod_name}.py")`
  then `_load("clean_experiment_downloads")`), and none is a WORKFLOW_INVARIANT
  member (checked against both the tuple and
  `tests/step9c_workflow_invariant_manifest.txt`), so invariant-exclusion is
  NOT the cause. The one that DOES map,
  `tests/test_janitor_noncanonical_caches.py`, differs only in carrying the
  contiguous repo-relative path literal `scripts/clean_experiment_downloads.py`
  in its module docstring (line 2) — which satisfies the literal arm. The two
  escaped tests reference the module by BARE NAME only
  (`clean_experiment_downloads.sweep_tmp_scratch`, no `scripts/` prefix, no
  `.py`). So the mapped test's coverage is incidental to a docstring path
  spelling, not designed: the real hole is the constructed-path loader whose
  only module reference is a bare module-name string. Filename naming
  ("feature-named, not module-named") is why the stem arm misses; the
  bare-name reference is why the literal arm misses. Both must hold for a
  consumer to escape, which is the shape a general fix should key on.
- `sweep_scope` is NOT a selector-emitted field: it lives entirely in the
  agent specs as a reporter-declared token —
  `.claude/agents/implementer.md` (items 1/1a + the Gate-scope-check report
  line), `.claude/agents/experiment-implementer.md` (fixed literal
  `selector-universe` on its path), `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md`
  (line ~1309, missing-token FAIL), `.claude/agents/codex-code-reviewer.md`,
  and `.claude/skills/issue/steps/08-step-4.md`. So scope item 3 is a
  spec-plus-gate change, not a selector change, and its two candidate
  mechanisms differ in blast radius: making the selector emit its realized
  universe (selector change, narrow) vs requiring the reporter to state the
  grep command and target set alongside the label (spec + reviewer-lens +
  possibly `workflow_lint.py` change, fleet-wide).
- Routing per the parent's note confirmed: not blocking #2336, filed
  separately because the selector is shared by every session's Step 9c gate.
